title: Hybrid prefetch + kernel fingerprinting to reduce embedding p99 for mixed workloads
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Reduce tail latency (p99/p999) on the embeddings endpoint for mixed-size workloads by combining a lightweight hybrid prefetcher, kernel fingerprinting for deterministic kernel routing, and a slow-path isolation policy. Current p99 regressions occur during bursty ingress and heterogeneous embedding sizes; the goal is to keep p99 within SLA while preserving median latency and overall throughput.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for standard 1024-dim embedding model on our N1 fleet improves from baseline by >=35% under mixed traffic simulated load
No >5% regression in median latency (p50) or throughput for steady-state workloads
New kernel routing produces deterministic routing decisions with <2% misroute rate in canary experiments
End-to-end e2e test coverage and a canary rollout plan exist in the console and are documented
steps: Instrument current request metadata and build a compact kernel fingerprint (sequence_len, batch_hint, input_size, quant_flag)
Implement hybrid prefetcher in the dispatcher: fast-path prefetch for high-confidence fingerprints, background speculative prefetch for low-confidence ones
Add a kernel fingerprint table that maps fingerprints to preferred kernel IDs and observed tail latency stats
Introduce a slow-path isolation queue that drains long-running or mismatched requests onto a dedicated shard to prevent head-of-line blocking
Benchmark on canary N1/N2 nodes across 3 workload mixes and compare p50/p95/p99/p999 with baseline
Iterate on hysteresis thresholds and prefetch TTL to balance extra memory usage vs latency wins
Create rollout plan: feature flag, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLA breach
recent_comments: 2026-03-03 - Ethan Chen: Initial spike: identified that 18% of p99 events correlated with kernel selection mismatch when sequence_len differs from queue-average. Captured additional request fields in logs for fingerprinting.
2026-03-05 - Priya Singh: Design review feedback: prefer compact 32-bit hash for fingerprint table to keep memory low; ask infra to confirm memory budget for N1 canaries.

2026-03-07 - Miguel Ramirez (runtime): Proof-of-concept prefetcher implemented. Microbench results: speculative prefetch reduces average KV cache miss penalty by ~25% for 512/1024 mixed workloads but increases memory churn under pathological bursts.

2026-03-09 - QA: Added e2e load scenario scripts and synthetic users to reproduce bursty ingress from customer A. Observed p99 baseline 460ms -> hybrid prefetch 280ms on A100 equivalent nodes during mixed bursts (prelim).
2026-03-11 - Design: Agreed to add conservative hysteresis and soft-fallback to non-prefetch path when memory pressure >70% to avoid OOMs.
2026-03-12 - Security: Quick review passed; no additional KMS or data exposure concerns for fingerprint metadata. Marked security_review_required=false.
estimated_impact: Expect 30-45% p99 reduction for mixed-size workloads and 20-30% fewer p999 spikes; resource cost increase is expected to be small (<5% memory) with configurable guardrails.
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation and kernel table lookup
Integration tests for prefetcher interactions with KV cache and scheduler (simulate cache misses)
Canary performance tests: 5% traffic for 48h with automated p99/p999 monitoring and rollback threshold at +10% over baseline
Chaos test: introduce random slow kernels and verify isolation queue prevents cluster-wide p99 degradation
Regression test against embedding quality: ensure no change to embedding outputs (deterministic kernels only)
